question: Is prophecy a sure thing?
summary: 2 Peter 1:19 calls the prophetic word more sure (bebaioteron) — a lamp shining in a dark place that the faithful do well to heed. Jeremiah 18:7-10 makes prophecy explicitly conditional: if Yahweh declares destruction against a nation and that nation repents, he will relent; if he declares blessing and that nation does evil, he will withdraw the blessing. 2 Peter treats prophecy as fixed and reliable; Jeremiah treats it as contingent on human response. The two passages disagree on whether prophetic announcements are predictions of fixed outcomes or conditional warnings.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read God's 'repentance' language as pertaining only to announced threatenings, which always carry an implicit condition, leaving his unconditional decree intact.

discrepancy.connective: Robert P. Carroll reads Jeremiah 18:7-10's conditionality as the tradition's own device for rationalizing failed threats, undercutting confidence that biblical prophecy was ever simply 'sure.'

skeptic.name: Robert P. Carroll
skeptic.work: When Prophecy Failed: Reactions and Responses to Failure in the Old Testament Prophetic Traditions
skeptic.attribution: Robert P. Carroll (1941-2000), When Prophecy Failed: Reactions and Responses to Failure in the Old Testament Prophetic Traditions (London: SCM Press, 1979)

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), p. 148
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley has a dedicated heading, 'Sure, yet not always fulfilled' (p. 148), pairing 2 Peter 1:19 and Deuteronomy 18:21-22 against Jonah 3:4-10's unfulfilled forty-day prophecy, and cites Jeremiah 18:7-10 by name, distinguishing its conditional 'promises and threatenings' from Deuteronomy's 'absolute predictions, which are in no way contingent upon human conduct.'

link.title: GotQuestions: What does it mean that we have a more sure word of prophecy (2 Peter 1:19)?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of the 2 Peter 1:19 side of the tension (the meaning of 'more sure'); does not itself engage Jeremiah 18's conditional-prophecy language.

excerpts.excerpt_text: When the Scripture attributeth repentance unto God, it is not that he doeth contrary to that which he hath ordained in his secret counsel: but when he threateneth, it is a calling to repentance, and when he giveth man grace to repent, the threatening (which ever containeth a condition in it) taketh no place: and this the scripture calleth repentance in God, because it so appeareth to man's judgment.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: The note explicitly distinguishes God's fixed 'secret counsel' from an announced 'threatening,' which 'ever containeth a condition in it' -- directly explaining why Jeremiah's conditional oracle need not undermine the claim that prophecy (2 Peter 1:19) is 'sure.'
